articles.title: Music Assistant brings local drives and network shares into one setup
articles.dek: A folder picker replaces typed paths, while existing network-share sources retain their libraries and access rules.
body: Music Assistant brings local folders, connected drives and network shares into one Local files setup. People can browse for a music folder instead of typing its server path, and household members allowed to add music sources can choose from storage made available by an administrator.

A Storage page under System manages those locations and shows which music sources use them. Existing SMB and NFS network-share sources convert to Local files at startup while keeping their libraries, playlists and access rules. In the Home Assistant app, their shares appear under the common media folder, where other apps can see them too.

Marcel van der Veldt also protects against treating an unavailable drive or share as an empty music folder. The conversion removes the old SMB cache mode; Home Assistant app installations can pin only SMB versions 1.0 or 2.0. Docker installations can use only folders mapped into their container.

articles.title: Home Assistant lets household members edit their own profile
articles.dek: Household members can update their own identity without asking an administrator.
body: Home Assistant lets each household member edit their own name and profile picture from an Edit profile button. Previously, changing a picture required an administrator to open that person’s settings. The new dialog uploads and crops an image and keeps the name consistent across the account and its linked person.

The permission covers only the signed-in person’s name and picture. Device tracking and account privileges stay under administrator control. Pictures must be uploaded to Home Assistant; accounts without an editable linked person can change their name but cannot set a picture.

articles.title: Home Assistant explores simpler phone actions and sensor controls
articles.dek: A dedicated companion-app integration would replace copied notification codes with guided actions while keeping personal sensors under the phone owner’s control.
body: Home Assistant is considering a dedicated integration for its official iOS and Android apps, with guided notification and phone-command controls instead of special values copied into configuration. A proposal published by Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves describes one place for a person’s mobile devices and actions that show only compatible targets.

The proposed design gives Home Assistant responsibility for how phone sensors and actions appear, while the apps report which capabilities they support. Enabling personal sensors would still require the phone owner’s consent in the app; another user could not silently switch on location tracking from Home Assistant.

The opportunity remains in Considering. It proposes an opt-in introduction alongside the existing mobile integration, followed by migration as the design matures. The communication contract, compatibility and transition still need work, and there is no committed timeline.

externalSources.title: Dedicated Core integration for the official companion apps (successor to mobile_app)

articles.title: ESPHome builds ESP8266 firmware without Rosetta on Apple Silicon
articles.dek: A new default build system speeds compilation, with an opt-out needed for custom frameworks and unlisted boards.
body: ESPHome changes the default build system for ESP8266 devices, using its own packaged compiler and Arduino framework instead of fetching them from the PlatformIO registry. Apple Silicon Macs run the compiler directly without Rosetta, and Device Builder gains a compilation percentage for these devices.

J. Nick Koston measured a fresh build without a compilation cache at 9.2 seconds instead of 17.8 on an M5 Max, using a configuration with networking, a web server, a sensor and a light. Tests of the compiler and framework packages produced firmware identical to the previous packages.

The first build after switching starts clean. Configurations using a custom framework source, a version other than 3.1.2 or an unlisted board must explicitly keep toolchain: platformio for now. Hosts outside the supported Linux, macOS and Windows builds also need an alternative. The PlatformIO route is deprecated for removal in 2027.4.0, when configurations still requiring it will stop building.

articles.title: ESPHome gives Zigbee sensors standard readings for other devices
articles.dek: Standard temperature, humidity and occupancy reports open a path to direct device bindings.
body: ESPHome gives makers an option to expose ESP32-based Zigbee sensors using the standard measurement formats understood by other devices. A temperature sensor can use Temperature Measurement instead of a generic input, opening the possibility of binding it directly to a compatible Zigbee thermostat.

Contributor luar123 adds formats for temperature, humidity, pressure, flow, light level, fine particles, carbon dioxide and occupancy. The option improves how ZHA and Zigbee2MQTT interpret reporting and measurement types, but does not automatically create a binding. Existing generic reports remain the default, and the standard formats do not carry custom sensor names.

articles.title: Local speech recognition keeps Cantonese distinct from Mandarin
articles.dek: OHF Voice corrects language choices and narrows the advertised list to the selected recognition backend.
body: OHF Voice’s Wyoming Faster Whisper service correctly routes Cantonese requests to supported speech-recognition backends. A Cantonese Home Assistant pipeline could previously fail to match the advertised language, and the Qwen3 backend could turn the request into Mandarin by dropping its region code.

Michael Hansen also makes the service report the languages its chosen backend supports instead of advertising the same large list for every engine. Regional language tags reach the appropriate engine, and an English-only Whisper model advertises English alone.
The reported list still has a limit: it does not fully reflect every manually selected alternative model, and adding a backend requires a server restart before the list changes.

pullRequests.title: Report the languages the configured backend can actually transcribe

articles.title: Music Assistant respects the account using a shared Plex server
articles.dek: Shared users avoid failed sign-ins and accidental connections with the server owner’s access.
body: Music Assistant corrects sign-in for people using a Plex server shared with their account. Falling back to an ordinary Plex account token could either fail setup or, on networks allowing unauthenticated access, connect in the server owner’s context instead of the shared user’s.

The connection verifies the chosen server and the user’s server-specific access before loading cached library information. A missing permission produces a clear access-denied error. Contributor aevans0001 makes a first contribution to the Music Assistant server, reviewed by Marvin Schenkel.

pullRequests.title: Fix Plex login for users the server is shared with

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps pairing open when a device goes quiet
articles.dek: Bluetooth and network discovery no longer withdraw a setup already being completed.
body: Home Assistant stops removing a device’s setup card while someone is entering its pairing code. Bluetooth devices can stop advertising as soon as a connection begins, so pairing itself could make the device disappear and end setup with an invalid-flow error.

J. Nick Koston extends the protection for an active setup to Bluetooth and SSDP network discovery. A device explicitly reporting that it is already paired still ends the attempt, and unplugged USB devices retain their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: Keep discovery flows the user is configuring when a device goes quiet

articles.title: Music Assistant loads large libraries in its mobile and car views
articles.dek: Smaller requests avoid oversized replies, and a new filter finds tracks within loaded lists.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app retrieves large libraries and queues in smaller pieces instead of asking for an entire collection in one reply. Oversized responses could never reach Android Auto, CarPlay, the add-to-playlist picker and queue refreshes because they exceeded the server’s message limit.

Andrii Mitnovych also adds a text filter within loaded playlist, album and podcast lists and an artist’s expanded track list. Removing a track from a filtered playlist uses its original playlist position, so the filtered row does not point at the wrong song.

pullRequests.title: Bound list payloads and add in-list track filter (#1010)

articles.title: Assist keeps identical commands in the room they came from
articles.dek: A remembered interpretation no longer carries one device’s room into another device’s request.
body: Assist stops reusing one device’s room when another device sends the same words. Requests that supplied a device identity without a satellite identity could share a remembered interpretation, causing a command that relies on its room context to use the first caller’s room.
Michael Hansen makes the saved result distinguish the originating device as well as the words and language.

pullRequests.title: Include device id in the conversation intent cache key

articles.title: Home Assistant restores sign-in through password managers
articles.dek: Firefox and password managers can find and submit the login fields again.
body: Home Assistant makes its login fields visible to password managers again, including Firefox’s built-in login manager. The fields had moved behind nested interface components that those tools could not find. Petar Petrov also lets a password manager submit the filled form as a login, verifying the correction in Firefox.

pullRequests.title: Render login fields in the light DOM so password managers can find them

articles.title: Home Assistant stops one text reading discarding a history batch
articles.dek: One address containing a line break no longer causes other readings to be lost in an InfluxDB export.
body: Home Assistant protects InfluxDB history exports from a single text reading containing a line break. A multiline address from a phone’s location sensor could cause the database to reject a whole batch, losing other devices’ state changes along with it. Franck Nijhof replaces line breaks inside text values with spaces before sending them.

pullRequests.title: Fix InfluxDB dropping a batch when a string field contains a line break

articles.title: Home Assistant withdraws the separate De Dietrich integration
articles.dek: The boiler connection is being reconsidered as part of a shared Modbus integration.
body: Home Assistant withdraws the separate De Dietrich boiler integration reported on September 15 before its first release. The planned connection provided local measurements from Diematic heating systems, without heating controls.

Daan Vervacke says the agreed direction is a shared integration for De Dietrich and Remeha Modbus devices, with each brand directing users to it. The removal avoids introducing a separate integration that would soon need replacing; it does not establish when the shared version will arrive.

pullRequests.title: Remove De Dietrich integration
Remove De Dietrich integration documentation

articles.title: ESPHome stops a five-second absence delay becoming 27 minutes
articles.dek: DFRobot presence sensors use the configured delay; old millisecond workarounds need correcting.
body: ESPHome corrects an output-delay setting for DFRobot SEN0395 presence sensors that could keep reporting a departed person for about 27 minutes. A configured five-second delay was passed as 5,000 seconds and then limited to the sensor’s maximum of 1,638.375 seconds.

Christopher Pruijsen fixes the unit conversion. Anyone who used the workaround of writing 5ms to obtain five seconds must change it back to 5s. Formulas that return a delay in seconds keep their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: [dfrobot_sen0395] Fix output_latency treating milliseconds as seconds

articles.title: Deleting a local music file keeps its streaming-service links
articles.dek: Music Assistant preserves favourites and playlist entries when another source still carries the track.
body: Deleting a local file no longer removes an entire Music Assistant library track when a streaming service still carries it. The next synchronization removes only the deleted file’s link, preserving the other source along with favourites, playlist entries and listening history.
The track still disappears when that file was its only source. Artwork and audio analysis supplied by the deleted file are removed with it.

pullRequests.title: Keep a track's other providers when its local file is deleted

roadmapUpdates.title: Two-way camera audio receives approval and High priority
roadmapUpdates.summary: Franck Nijhof approves two-way camera audio and marks it High priority; transferring the iOS app to foundation ownership also gains High priority and takes precedence. Timothy proposes using the companion app’s microphone for local HTTP connections while keeping video and controls in the web interface; echo cancellation still needs testing and native call-style notifications remain outside the first step.

roadmapUpdates.summary: The dashboard-section opportunity moves from Approved to Building. Its first step aims to generate an area-filtered section that follows matching devices automatically; status filters and individual exceptions remain later work.

roadmapUpdates.title: Radio reception becomes high-priority work
roadmapUpdates.summary: Receiving radio-frequency commands moves from Approved to Now with High priority. The opportunity concerns bringing received signals into Home Assistant; the planning change does not establish a release.

roadmapUpdates.title: Matter cameras get one narrower first-step plan
roadmapUpdates.summary: Matthias Kerstner consolidates the first Matter camera plan into one opportunity in Building, proposing setup, live streaming and panning through the existing camera interface. The earlier umbrella item is marked Done because of that consolidation; full pan/tilt/zoom, two-way audio and interface refinements remain separate work, with no release established.

sources.title: Support Matter cameras using the existing camera UI
Make Matter cameras feel like an established camera integrations

roadmapUpdates.title: A Matter compatibility audit moves into Building
roadmapUpdates.summary: The comparison of the Matter specification, Matter.js implementation and reference SDK moves from Now to Building. It aims to identify gaps for future priorities, without adding device features by itself.

sources.title: Synchronize Matter specification against Matter server implementation and SDK to deduct gaps and opportunities

roadmapUpdates.title: Trigger-reference completion waits on a documentation check
roadmapUpdates.summary: Franck Nijhof pauses marking the trigger-reference opportunity complete after questioning whether documentation is still missing, and asks Ashley Abbott to check. The opportunity remains in Building.

sources.title: Improve referencing triggers in automation conditions and actions

roadmapUpdates.title: Web-server settings work drops to Medium priority
roadmapUpdates.summary: Franck Nijhof lowers web-server configuration from Critical to Medium priority after its first phase, making room for work such as the installer. The remaining opportunity stays in Building.

sources.title: HTTP server configuration through the UI (removing port 8123)

roadmapUpdates.title: Native iPhone detail sheets get a separate proposal
roadmapUpdates.summary: Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves opens a narrower Considering opportunity for native sheets and navigation bars around existing entity details. It keeps the frontend’s dialog content, separates this work from bottom-tab navigation, and proposes an App Labs introduction before wider rollout; Android implementation is outside this first scope.

sources.title: Give the companion app platform-standard navigation
Give the companion app platform-standard navigation (Modal presentations and top navigation bar)

roadmapUpdates.title: The broad Zigbee opportunity leaves the roadmap board
roadmapUpdates.summary: The broad Zigbee-support opportunity is removed from the public roadmap board. Related Green Power and transition work now reference the foundation’s goals repository; this change does not establish cancellation or completion.

sources.title: Further shape Zigbee support by implementing missing features in ZHA while retaining choice
Pre-work for enabling further shaping of Zigbee support
